body:
Carlyle Credit Income Fund (NYSE:CCIF) is scheduled to report fiscal third-quarter 2026 results on Aug 20, with Wall Street bracing for a period marked by sharply reduced expectations across both revenue and earnings forecasts.

Analysts expect the closed-end fund to post revenue of $5.39 million for the quarter, with earnings of $0.09 per share, according to consensus estimates compiled by GuruFocus. Full-year 2026 revenue is projected at $23.7 million with earnings of $0.37 per share.

The upcoming report comes against a backdrop of significant downward revisions. Over the past 90 days, full-year 2026 revenue estimates have been cut from $30.01 million to $23.7 million, while 2027 revenue projections dropped even more dramatically, from $41.8 million to $25.28 million. Earnings per share estimates for 2026 have fallen from $0.52 to $0.37, and 2027 estimates declined from $0.53 to $0.49.

The fund's most recent quarterly results, for the period ended March 31, 2026, underscored the challenges facing the credit-focused investment vehicle. Actual revenue of $5.54 million missed analyst expectations of $7.19 million by roughly 23%, while earnings of $0.09 per share fell short of the $0.13 consensus estimate by more than 30%. Despite the misses, shares edged up 0.93% in the following trading session.

Despite the shrinking estimates, analyst positioning remains constructive. Three analysts covering the fund have set one-year price targets averaging $3.75, with a high of $4.00 and a low of $3.50. At the current trading price of $2.84, that average target implies potential upside of approximately 32%.

The consensus recommendation from four brokerage firms stands at 2.30 on a five-point scale, corresponding to an Outperform rating. On this scale, 1 represents Strong Buy and 5 represents Sell.

Investors will be closely monitoring whether the fund can stabilize its revenue trajectory after last quarter's sizable shortfall. The steep downward revisions for 2027 suggest analysts have grown more cautious about the fund's near-term growth prospects, even as the average price target still points to meaningful upside from current levels.

GuruFocus has flagged three warning signs for the fund, though specific details on those indicators were not disclosed in the preview. The research platform also noted that investors can access more detailed estimate data through its forecast pages and use its DCF calculator to assess valuation.

Carlyle Credit Income Fund operates as a closed-end fund focused on credit investments, providing exposure to a portfolio of credit instruments under the Carlyle umbrella. The earnings release will offer the first comprehensive look at whether the fund's performance has improved since the March quarter shortfall.

Note: The earnings report date is Aug 20, 2026, based on the most recent preview. An earlier version of the preview cited Aug 19, 2026, and referenced a slightly different current share price of $2.89, which would imply upside of approximately 30% from the $3.75 average target.
